glosses: An individual consignment of cargo for shipment, regardless of size and form.
An individual item appearing on an invoice or receipt (only in the phrase bill of parcels).
A division of land bought and sold as a unit.

examples.text: I own a small parcel of land between the refinery and the fish cannery.

glosses: An indiscriminate or indefinite number, measure, or quantity; a collection; a group.

examples.text: […] this youthful parcel / Of noble bachelors stand at my bestowing,
[…] instead of sitting (as she ought to have done) by her good father and mother, she must needs run up into the gallery, and sit with a parcel of giddy creatures of her own age […]

glosses: A small amount of food that has been wrapped up, for example a pastry.
A portion of anything taken separately; a fragment of a whole; a part.

examples.text: A certain piece of land is part and parcel of another piece.

glosses: To wrap something up into the form of a package.
To wrap a strip around the end of a rope.

examples.text: Worm and parcel with the lay; turn and serve the other way.

glosses: To divide and distribute by parts or portions; often with off, out or into.

examples.text: Their woes are parcell’d, mine are general.

glosses: To add a parcel or item to; to itemize.

examples.text: […] that mine own servant should / Parcel the sum of my disgraces by / Addition of his envy!

glosses: Part or half; in part; partially.
